doc.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019

title: Where germs come from: Times Square and picking up pulses
summary: Examples such as driving to Florida and writing in London, plus Dizzy asking how he is so prolific and a movie publishing dispute.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: No. Well there’s more than one way to get a germ. Like there’s been times when I’ve been playing something, practicing, and at the end some kind of accident would happen. I say oh wait, that’s something. And then I would capture that and then would go write a piece of music based on it. But once I started writing, forget the piano. Other times — I remember once I was driving to Florida in a snowstorm. And it was snowing from New York all the way to St. Augustine, Florida. And down south, they don’t know how to deal with snow, right? And so it was bumper to bumper traffic the whole way down there. And so finally the sun was out and I was pulling in the driveway with my parents, and I started hearing in my head [scats]. I said, oh man, I’m hearing this thing and it was New York, Times Square. And so my mother went to hug me and I ran past her and got a piece of manuscript paper. And I recorded that. It’s called “Times Square.” It’s on one of my albums.

And Dizzy asked me once, on an airplane, he said, “Man, how do you be so prolific?” And I’m saying why is he asking me that, I never wrote anything like “Con Alma” or something like that. Then I realized he was serious. So I said sometimes I’ll be looking at the piano and I’ll just go over and play a chord. Other times I’ll hear a melody in my head. Another time I’ll be thinking of a rhythm and a melody starts to happen. And at one point Dizzy took me to Lalo Schifrin’s home for dinner. And I was just with him for a couple of months and I see Lalo in this big mansion. And I said maybe I’d better think about writing for movies. That’s what Lalo did. And so I got to where I could pick up a pulse from — I remember once writing in London. I was in this basement — in the room I was in the basement of the hotel, so you could see the kids coming out of this elementary school. So I tried to pick up the pulse from that and write a piece of music. It was eventually recorded and it became a commercial for the Miami Dolphins football team.

But I didn’t write it for that but it was a real piece of music. So I can pick up a pulse. I could write West End Avenue and 101st Street at 3:30 in the afternoon just by going to listen to the traffic and how it’s moving. And I pick a pulse and the pulse presents a melody to me and that’s the way I would have written for a movie. I did write one movie but I had a fight with the producer. They wanted my publishing. They wanted to take all my publishing rights. I said no deal.
